paragraphs: Oshaya of Terya. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Bava Kamma: Abba Oshaya was a washerman, his clothes made from a different kind of wool so people would not accuse him of theft. He returned lost property to a gentile for sanctification of the Name, being pious (Jerusalem Talmud, Ellu Metzi'ot). When he died they saw his bier fly in the air; his generation applied to him, “If a man gives all his house’s wealth for love,” Vayikra Rabbah 30. He was born the day Rabbi Avin died, Midrash Kohelet on “The sun rises.” When Abba Oshaya died, Rabbi Yehoshua his son was born; so Yuchasin writes in Midrash Shmuel’s name. But Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of Chayyei Sarah, lacks “his son.” Yuchasin gave him a separate entry.
